headline: High-dimensional immune profiling is resolving disease-specific host molecular states
label: Immune Profiling Disease Signatures
summary: Transcriptomic, mass cytometry and proteomic profiling now separate febrile infection types, lupus immune signaling and trauma responses in molecular detail.
synthesis: The common thread is resolving host immune heterogeneity at cellular or molecular resolution to define disease-specific states. The most substantial quantitative evidence is a multi-cohort blood transcriptomic study in febrile children (n=1,683 microarray, n=767 RNA-seq, dPCR confirmation) yielding signatures that separate viral, bacterial and inflammatory disease. In systemic lupus erythematosus, mass cytometry captures unperturbed in vivo immune signaling, addressing patient heterogeneity directly. Trauma profiling describes coordinated innate, adaptive, neuroendocrine and metabolic responses in humans. Methodological advances include reframing immune cell doublets from artifacts toward informative events and a sensitive secretome method for rare cells in complex tissue. Autoinflammatory disease work evaluates CRP and composite indices against multi-modal omics, while EV proteomics and microfluidic red cell storage quality control extend the theme to vesicle and transfusion contexts. The novelty lies in pairing high-dimensional readouts with specific disease or cell-state questions, though the set is heterogeneous.
